tasks.task: Turn a crowded deck or notes into a slide-by-slide plan

items.when: When a talk, pitch or training deck is due and you start from notes or a crowded deck
When each slide must make one point with a sentence headline, a layout type and zones
Before the slide plan, to set an outline that builds belief and ends in a clear ask
When every slide is a title and bullets, to get three hand-made alternatives
When the plan is agreed and the client wants a storyboard and a PowerPoint file from it
Before the deck is presented or shared, to catch low contrast and missing titles
When the deck lists facts in order and has no story or request

tasks.task: Fix a slide that says too much

items.when: When a slide has too much text, two messages or a heading that says nothing
When words could become a picture, to plan a visual that pairs with a short line
When the text must lose words without losing the point
When the slide is rebuilt, to see where the eye lands first and what to cut
When the slide is really a document and the detail belongs in a handout

tasks.task: Write the story and slide text for a new deck

items.when: When the story is set and each slide needs its headline and what goes where
When the order is open, to get an arc for this audience and this decision to react to
When the deck rests on numbers, to turn them into the point, the proof and the next step
When the source is a long report, to put the answer and the decision on one opening slide
When the draft runs long, to test slide count, talk time and type size

tasks.task: Design an investor pitch deck

items.when: When the founder has the content and needs a layout where each slide makes one point
When every claim needs a dated source in a backup section
When the deck must be a PowerPoint file with real editable text, tables and charts
Before it is sent, to score slide count, length and type size and get a cut list
When the deck has thirty slides and the purpose is not clear by slide two

tasks.task: Design a sales or customer deck

items.when: When the sales story is known and each slide needs its layout and headline
When the deck follows an audit, to turn findings into a ten-slide story with proof
When the buyer may want a one-pager or leave-behind in place of a full deck
Before it goes to a client, to find number mismatches, weak wording and format slips

tasks.task: Make visual-first slides for a talk or webinar

items.when: When the talk is written and the slides should carry pictures and few words
When it is a webinar that must teach one clear result, with outline and deck
When the client wants to see a version with one drawn image per slide
When the talk comes from a finished paper and needs slides, notes and a script
When the slides are light and the speaker needs notes, transitions and timings
Before the talk, to check the slides read from the back of the room and on a small screen
When the speaker plans to read the slides aloud

tasks.task: Choose and style a chart for a slide or page

items.when: When you have numbers and need the right chart, styled so it says one thing
When the chart must be drawn cleanly from the client's own data
When the deck holds charts as pictures and they must become editable charts
When a chart is drafted, to check the chart type and axes do not mislead
When numbers come from a workbook, to check each slide figure agrees with it
When the chart shows everything and the audience cannot see what to look at

tasks.task: Build a slide or document template a team can reuse

items.when: When a team needs one size, grid, type scale, colours and master layouts to build from
When the team has no fonts set, to compare three pairs with sizes and line spacing
When the look is open, to see the same slides in several themes before fixing one
When the choices are made, to write firm rules for colour, type and grid
When the template is built, to fill it with real content and see where layouts break
Before the template is shared, to check every text and background pair

tasks.task: Build the deck as an editable file

items.when: When the plan is approved and the client needs a PowerPoint file they can edit
When the client has their own template and approved content to pour into it
When the deck will be shown in a browser and could use motion
When a deck must change from 4:3 to 16:9 with no stretched images
When the file is built, to get it ready to present and to share
When the client wants a fast first draft from an outline to react to

tasks.task: Review a deck and list the fixes

items.when: When the review finds slides with two messages or empty headings
When the deck carries figures, to check numbers, wording and format slide by slide
When there is an old and a new version, to list every changed message, number and link
When the deck will be shared, for fixes to titles, reading order and alternative text

tasks.task: Check a deck, workbook or PDF for accessibility

items.when: Before anything is presented, shared or published, to catch what stops people reading it
When the file is PowerPoint, for slide titles, reading order and alternative text
When colours are in doubt, to check each pair and get the nearest passing colour
When the piece is mostly text, to check size, spacing and line length

tasks.task: Turn a report or spreadsheet into a deck

items.when: Before any slide, to cut the report to the answer, the impact and the decision
When the source is a written report and the result must be an editable deck
When the source is a data file that must be cleaned and checked first
When the deck is built, to trace each slide number back to the workbook

tasks.task: Lay out a workbook or worksheet

items.when: When pages are filled in by hand or on screen and need space, order and clear prompts
When a Google Doc must look designed, to set a grid, a short type list and white space
When every page looks like a default document, to get three hand-made alternatives
When pages are drafted, to check type, spacing and line length where they are read

tasks.task: Lay out a lead magnet or checklist PDF

items.when: When a checklist or guide must print cleanly and read well on a phone
When the content is not settled, to pick a guide or checklist worth an email address
When the client also needs the path from the download to a sale
When one page could be a picture, to try an infographic version
When the layout is agreed and the PDF must be made with its layout checked
When the PDF is built from a web page and pages break badly or text prints blurry

tasks.task: Lay out an ebook interior

items.when: When a long document needs page size, margins, heading styles and a repeatable chapter opening
When the author has no fonts, to compare three pairs for long reading
When pages mix text, pull quotes and pictures and need one grid
When a sample chapter is set, to check line length and spacing for long reading
When the pages are decorated and the reader's path through them is unclear

tasks.task: Lay out a media kit or rate card

items.when: When a creator needs a 2 to 6 page kit using only the numbers and rates they supply
When numbers, partner logos and rates must sit on one tidy grid
When the kit looks like every other creator's, to get three hand-made alternatives
When a page is drafted, to check the eye lands on the number that matters

tasks.task: Design a printable or online business form

items.when: When a job sheet, order or inspection form must be filled in right first time
When the form will be built in an online tool and needs a field-by-field build list
When the form lives on a website and needs fields, error messages and spam protection
When the form is long, to compare a staged version with progress cues
When each reply should send an alert or log a row
When fields need help text and error messages in plain, polite words
When people fill the form in wrong and the form, not the people, is at fault

tasks.task: Redesign a form that comes back half-filled

items.when: When the old form must be rebuilt with every field justified
When you have the current form, to get a shorter field list, a new flow and a test script
When you know which fields go wrong, to find what in the design misleads people

tasks.task: Lay out a full book cover: front, spine and back

items.when: When a self-published book needs a cover that a printer or print-on-demand service will accept
Before the artist starts or after a printer rejects a file, to work out spine width and wrap size
When you need type zones, sizes and the full wrap laid out on the printer's template
Before layout, to find the one idea, one feeling and one symbol the cover should carry
When there is no art, to try a type-only cover that reads small
When the front is drafted, to test what reads at thumbnail size in an online store

tasks.task: Brief a cover illustrator or write AI cover prompts

items.when: When the illustrator needs the type zones and what the art must leave clear
When an illustrator needs one clear brief for the job
When one cover idea should be tried as four different treatments
When a prompt needs subject, light, style and a leave-out list for a named image tool
When the art comes back with faults, to turn each into a prompt line and a check
When you want to explore cover moods and then reuse the style chosen

tasks.task: Set a series look for several books

items.when: When each book in the series needs the same zones with its own title and art
When the series needs fixed type, colour and position rules for every future cover
When the series look is undecided, to compare three directions
When a direction is picked, to write what stays fixed and what changes per book

tasks.task: Make social graphics for a book or deck launch

items.when: When the launch needs a carousel, to plan the hook and the slide order
When a post needs a picture and you want a prompt, the exact size and a file plan
Before you settle the post layout, to get three hand-made alternatives
When a graphic is drafted, to check the title is what the eye lands on first

tasks.task: Draw a diagram or visual for a slide or page

items.when: Before drawing, to plan which visual pairs with the words so the point sticks
When a process or system needs a clean diagram you can reuse
When the content should be one infographic with a layout picked to fit it
When the visual carries data, to check it does not mislead

always.when: Before any deck or document that must match the client's live site: colours, fonts and voice
Before any file is presented, printed or published, to catch typos and names spelt two ways
When a slide or page states a number or claim you cannot trace to the client

helpers.when: When the talk itself needs writing, not only its slides
When the pitch needs its numbers, ask and investor story worked out
When the deck depends on many charts or a dashboard
When the launch needs flyers, posters or a full social set
When there is no brand palette or type to build the template from
When the ebook or workbook text needs editing before layout

gaps: No library item lays out an ebook or long document interior: chapter openings, running heads and page styles
No library item lays out a book cover or works out spine width from a printer's formula; only the kit does
No library item lays out a media kit or rate card
No library item designs a printable paper form such as a job sheet or inspection form; form items are for web forms
No library item lays out a workbook or worksheet with fill-in space
No library item builds slide masters, or covers Google Slides or Keynote; the deck items are for PowerPoint
No library item shows one deck in two or three visual directions as real slides to compare
No library item checks a PDF for tags, reading order and alternative text
No library item checks a print file for bleed, embedded fonts and image resolution
No library item sets a matching look across a book series
